script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for March 7. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
We walk on it without a thought.  Dirt.  Soil.

A single teaspoon of healthy soil contains up to 1 billion bacteria, yards of fungal threads, thousands of protozoa, and dozens of nematodes. You're standing on the most densely populated ecosystem on Earth. Without decomposers, dead matter would pile up forever.  Forests would be buried in their own leaves.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: The most important work often happens out of sight.  The billions of soil organisms ask no recognition yet make all visible life possible.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Underground Work - Honor the Invisible.

Here's your activity: Identify someone whose essential work usually goes unnoticed—maybe someone who maintains systems, cleans up, or supports behind the scenes. Thank them today. Like soil organisms, they make visible life possible. This helps you recognize and appreciate unseen essential work.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about what's living in the dirt can be applied to underground work - honor the invisible. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
